findings.description: The security group permits TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts against the instance.
The egress rule allows all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration path and command-and-control channel from the compromised host.

The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in plain text; user data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstances or from the instance metadata service, leaking long-lived static credentials.
No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 remains enabled and an SSRF in the web application could retrieve instance credentials without authentication.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance root EBS volume may store data at rest unencrypted.

The instance is launched into a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a route to an internet gateway, giving it a public address directly reachable from the internet rather than being placed in a private network layer.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so attached data is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so backup data is also stored without encryption and can be shared or restored without key-based control.
The VPC flow log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (SSE-KMS or customer-managed key), leaving sensitive network audit data unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy restrictions are defined for the flow-log bucket, risking public or cross-account exposure of network telemetry.
Audit log storage has no versioning, so flow log objects can be overwritten or deleted without recoverability, undermining the integrity of the audit trail.

findings.issue_category: force destroy on audit log bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true allows the log archive bucket and all stored flow log evidence to be deleted in a single terraform destroy, weakening audit trail durability.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, placing workloads directly on the internet rather than behind a NAT or load balancer.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, exposing resources that may not require inbound internet access.

The VPC's default security group is never explicitly restricted with an aws_default_security_group resource, so it may permit intra-group traffic that an explicitly authored group would not (CIS networking control).
